title: October 20: BrainBox — material memory, temporal transmission and a physical teaching loop
summary: Two branches turn Mad Monday's return-path intuition into simulated material mechanisms. Sol's supervised medium retains learned conductances after fast reset (4,000/4,000), reward-only learning fails its 80% gate (75%; reversed mapping 50% on every seed), and history crosses an engineered temporal port (1,279/1,280). Claude separates content from bridge-defined addresses, repairs bridge drift by interface totals, then trains PhiWorld-derived routing. Its computed-teacher G8b learns all three routes on three independent seeds; G9 moves the teaching interaction into one sequential field but gets 14/18 routes over two taught mappings and misses its reliability criterion. Physical gradient-signal agreement, correct task teaching and digital-AI advantage remain separate claims. Source results inspected, not independently rerun.

nodes.claim: Persistent positive conductances store experience separately from fast activity; identical later probes can expose that experience and transmit it through a temporal current into a frozen second medium.
nodes.survived: Locked supervised learning: 4,000/4,000 decisions after activity reset; frozen/erased/traffic-only 50%, shuffled 50.33%. A separate label-free history writer plus offline charge/energy matching and calibrated receiver transmits history at 1,279/1,280 (99.92%); fixed/erased 50%, shuffled 50.70%. Classical transient response models expose differences hidden from static DC. All experiment branches are integrated into main. October 21: exact locked training reproduces 20 writers; repair reduces independent-drift target error by 95.77%. Local-slowness retention is 99.79% versus 96.77% for the equal-state trace.
nodes.killed: Reward-only global perturbation learning fails the 80% gate: 75% overall, with the informative reversed mapping at 50% on every fresh seed. Six-parameter linear learning matches supervised accuracy much more cheaply. Raw charge alone transmits history at 100%, and matched-waveform peak at 96.64%; no universal scalar blindness or need for the full waveform is shown. Offline matching and supervised receiver calibration are explicit costs. Local writes do not generally beat global writes; drift protection needs more than phase gating. October 21: both corruption-training benefits fail; combined target error exceeds repair alone. Slowness replacement is 65.10% versus 100%, with all errors reading the old class; noise-off nearly ties retention.
nodes.era: October 20: persistent material and a temporal boundary

nodes.claim: Tests geometry-derived spectral addresses, interface-total stability and label-directed routing in a PhiWorld-derived medium, then moves the teaching interaction into sequential free/nudged/echo phases.
nodes.survived: Bridge drift and interior drift dissociate address and content; conserving redundant interface totals removes about 94–99% of drift damage in selected weak-bridge settings. Computed-teacher G8b learns a crossing 3×3 mapping on 3/3 independent variational-medium seeds. G9's second-harmonic local signal correlates 0.86–0.92 with a settled computed field-product reference. The sequential teacher learns 7/9 routes on each of two supplied mappings (14/18 combined); re-born fast field retains 6/9, shuffled slow material 1/9 on the primary mapping. October 21: G10a identifies wavelength-scale scattering texture rather than smooth wires. G11 redundant-interface repair removes 97–99% of drift damage. G12 separates ordered-domain and melted-sea noise responses.
nodes.killed: G9 misses its ≥2/3-perfect-seeds criterion: 1/3 perfect per mapping. No-clock gets 5/9 routes, so an accuracy advantage is unresolved at three seeds, despite stronger clocked transmission. Labels, clock, phase schedule, global update normalization and total-material projection remain supplied. G8b used incompletely settled fields; its exact-gradient description was corrected. Original PhiWorld linearization is nonreciprocal; the energy-derived variant restores symmetry but measured reciprocity retains 3–4% residual. Fixed slots match PAC over equal spans. Bit-matched snapshots beat drift repair; geometric continual learning loses to matched-rank GPM (48.6% vs 55.3%, 5/5 seeds). No digital-AI advantage established. October 21: G11 noise-aware writing adds no robustness benefit in its protocol. Neither a clean Bragg grating nor universal noise-created mass/slower time is established; mode frequency and propagation coefficient differ.
nodes.era: October 20: geometry, reciprocity and teaching inside the medium

edges.why: BrainBoxSol explicitly carries the October 19 hidden-branch/return-path question into persistent conductances and boundary responses; no direct cable-code inheritance is claimed.
BrainBoxSol explicitly connects its conductance writer to GrowingMatrix's local voltage-drop sensitivities and material-constrained optimization.
The source explicitly connects write selectivity, interference and direct-address controls; the different graph memories do not share an established performance advantage.
BrainBoxClaude names the Mad Monday return-ping discussion as motivation, then tests the extra conditions under which a return field can teach.

Claude's G4 explicitly ports Sol's 973bb63 medium and writer in brainbox/solport.py, reproduces the drift failure, and tests redundant-interface repair. The later wave teacher is a separate implementation.
Sol's phase/bridge synthesis explicitly tests Claude G2/G3 ideas on its medium: phase timing improves access but interface totals, rather than PAC alone, protect responses under bridge drift.

motifs.title: Experience changes material; a probe turns it into a new event
motifs.description: Persistent conductances or slow material remain after fast-state reset. Sol additionally transmits history through an engineered temporal port. Readout calibration, transport conditioning and cheap scalar alternatives count as parts of the mechanism.

motifs.title: A return becomes teaching only through the right dynamics and objective
motifs.description: Separate a history-carrying response from a learning sensitivity. Sol supplies a supervised adjoint; Claude needs reciprocity, labels, phase-sensitive sensing and settled contrastive phases. Agreement with a field-product reference is different from reliable task learning.

motifs.title: A useful simulated material mechanism still faces cheaper digital controls
motifs.description: Linear classifiers, scalar port summaries, fixed time slots, weight snapshots and learned protected subspaces limit the stronger claims. Geometry has measurable effects without establishing a digital AI advantage.
